title: El depósito
goal: Understand the deposit and when you get it back
culture: A month held as a deposit, in cash, with nothing written down. It comes back if the room does, and the time to settle what that means is now — pleasantly, while everybody still likes each other.

beats.es: Ah, y me deja el depósito.
beats.good: El depósito. Nothing is written down, so what it is and when it comes back are things you settle out loud, now.

beats.es: Un mes. Igual que el alquiler.
beats.good: One month’s rent, held in a drawer. Repeating the number is how a spoken agreement gets made in a country that does not sign much.

beats.objective: Ask when you get it back
beats.en: Do I get it back when I leave?
ok: me lo devuelve cuando me vaya
beats.good: Cuando me vaya — when I go. Ask it now, kindly, while the two of you are still pleased with each other.

beats.es: Cuando se vaya, sí. Si me deja el cuarto bien.
beats.good: Quedamos así — the same two words that closed the deal with the porter in the market. It is how every agreement in this country gets signed.
